html:
Joshua Nkomo was the leader of the Zimbabwe African People's Union and a founder of Zimbabwean nationalism, known as Father Zimbabwe.

A trade unionist and social worker, he led the nationalist movement from the 1950s, was jailed by the Rhodesian government for ten years, and led ZAPU's guerrilla army from Zambia in the Bush War.

He lost the 1980 election to Robert Mugabe, whose base was larger among the Shona majority. Mugabe sacked him in 1982, and his supporters were targeted in the Gukurahundi. He fled abroad for a time, then signed the Unity Accord of 1987 and became vice president. He died in 1999 and was buried at Heroes' Acre in Harare, Zimbabwe.
